title: Hybrid materialized cursors for low-latency dashboard explorations and incremental pagination
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Dashboard 'Explore' and paginated time-series panels exhibit high p50/p95 latencies when users page through result sets or apply ad-hoc filters. Current cursor-based pagination does not align with our shard layout and frequently re-executes expensive aggregation ranges. This manifests as inconsistent latency spikes and increased egress to the analytics pipeline for repeated queries.

Goal: Design and implement a hybrid materialized cursor mechanism that: (1) materializes lightweight, shard-aligned aggregates for recent time windows and hot segments, (2) encodes shard-aware resume tokens to avoid expensive re-scans, and (3) applies adaptive page sizing + prefetch planning to keep tail latency low while controlling backend work.

Why different from previous work: Existing tickets optimized index access patterns and caching across the board; this work combines incremental materialization (micro-aggregates kept in a short-lived store) with cursor semantics so the Console can offer low-latency exploration without inflating upstream storage queries or duplicating full materialized views. It is targeted at interactive UX patterns (explore/pivot/paginate) rather than batch analytics queries.
acceptance_criteria: P50 latency for first page of 1k-row exploration reduced to <= 150ms in US regions for typical tenant of 50k events/day
P95 latency reduced by at least 40% compared to baseline for 1..5 page navigation under 200 concurrent users
No functional regressions in ordering or cursor-resume semantics (existing API contract preserved)
Rollout path: feature flag gated + canary on 5% of traffic with metrics and automatic rollback on error budget breaches
Migration: no offline full-table rebuilds; new materialized micro-aggregates created incrementally and TTL-ed after 6 hours by default
benchmarks: Spike experiment (2026-02-25): single-node bench w/ 10k event tenant: baseline p50=360ms, p95=1.2s; hybrid prototype p50=118ms (67% drop), p95=680ms (43% drop)
Cost estimate (on prototype workload): backend query CPU cycles down ~28% for interactive paging workload; network bytes saved ~22% due to reduced re-fetches
Memory: micro-aggregates add ~18MB per hot-shard under our simulated tenant; TTL keeps steady-state overhead bounded
implementation_notes:
High-level plan: 1) Introduce micro-aggregate store (Redis cluster) keyed by tenant_id + time-bucket + segment-hash. Each entry stores pre-aggregated top-k and counts for the bucket. 2) Update Dashboard query planner to consult materialized store for recent buckets and stitch results with historical index reads for older buckets. 3) Encode cursor as base64(parts: last-seen-key, shard-id, time-bucket, materialize-flag, checksum) so resume logic is shard-aware. 4) Adaptive page sizing: client requested 'page_size' becomes a soft hint; server may return fewer items for extremely expensive pages and include prefetch token to fetch next chunk. 5) Fallback: if materialized store miss or checksum mismatch, fall back to deterministic index scan; instrument to record miss rates. 6) Rollout: feature-flagged boolean in tenant config; start with 5% canary then 25% then 100%. 7) Telemetry: add metrics: materialize_hit, materialize_miss, cursor_rewrite_rate, page_size_adjustments, stitch_latency. 8) Migration: background writer pipeline consumes analytics stream and populates micro-aggregates for recent windows; TTL = 6h, configurable.

Technical trade-offs considered: using existing shard cache vs new Redis store (chosen Redis for predictable TTL and eviction), fully materializing top-k vs storing sketches (top-k chosen to preserve ordering semantics), encoding cursor with checksum to detect schema drift (adds 20 bytes but prevents silent errors).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Stale micro-aggregates cause inconsistent ordering across pages; Mitigation: include a server-side consistency window and checksum in cursor; if mismatch, force full rescan and surface a warning metric
Risk: Redis cost/pressure under high tenancy; Mitigation: TTL + eviction + backpressure to fall back to index scans and autoscale Redis cluster for canary
Risk: Edge-case filters that require non-groupable expressions; Mitigation: categorize queries — materialize only groupable aggregations; others default to existing path
